publications.title: ElecLoad: Adaptive Electricity Load Forecasting Guided by Multiple Events
publications.abstract: Accurate electricity load forecasting provides critical decision support for energy procurement, generation scheduling, and supply-demand balancing, contributing to the economic efficiency and operational reliability of power systems. However, future electricity demand can be affected by the complex interplay of multiple events described in Web notices, weather alerts, and event schedules. Their effects vary over time and can reinforce or offset one another, making electricity load difficult to forecast accurately. While existing methods can incorporate context as additional input, how to use the effects of multiple events and their interactions to guide the load forecasting process itself remains to be explored. To address this gap, we propose ElecLoad, a context-aware agent for multi-event electricity load forecasting that adaptively organizes the forecasting process. Specifically, we train ElecLoad to combine historical load with context to analyze each event's relevance to the target load, the timing of its effects, and potential interactions among events. Guided by this analysis, ElecLoad adaptively chooses to forecast the entire forecast horizon directly or to partition it into segments according to changes in event effects. When the horizon is partitioned, sub-agents independently generate initial forecasts for each segment. The main agent then reviews these forecasts, and the sub-agents perform selective refinement guided by its feedback. Experiments on multiple electricity load datasets show that ElecLoad achieves state-of-the-art performance in most evaluation scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/zhjai/ElecLoad.

publications.title: The Role of Microsoft Excel in Supporting Data-Driven Economic Decision-Making Among MSME Actors in The Digital
publications.abstract: This article examines the role of Microsoft Excel in supporting data-driven economic decision-making among micro, small, and medium-sized enterprise (MSME) actors in the digital era. The study uses a qualitative literature review by synthesizing academic publications on spreadsheet-based financial recording, digital adoption, accounting information systems, financial literacy, and managerial decision-making. The review indicates that Excel can help MSMEs organize transaction records, summarize sales and expenses, calculate costs and profit, monitor cash flows, manage inventory, compare business performance, and prepare simple financial projections. Functions such as SUM, AVERAGE, IF, SUMIF, sorting, filtering, charts, and PivotTables can convert routine records into information that is easier to interpret. Such information may support decisions concerning pricing, purchasing, stock replenishment, cost control, promotion, and business expansion. Nevertheless, Excel does not automatically guarantee sound decisions. The usefulness of its outputs depends on the completeness, accuracy, consistency, and timeliness of the input data, as well as the user's spreadsheet competence and basic financial literacy. Risks include formula errors, duplicate or missing transactions, uncontrolled file versions, and inadequate data security. The article concludes that Excel is best positioned as an accessible transitional and supporting tool within a broader digital financial-management process, not as a substitute for accounting standards, internal controls, or professional judgment.

publications.title: Beyond Benchmark Accuracy: A Hybrid Framework for Phishing URL and Email Detection
publications.abstract: Phishing detectors can achieve almost perfect accuracy on benchmark datasets and still struggle with the links people encounter in practice. This paper investigates that gap and describes a hybrid framework for assessing URLs and emails through machine learning, language analysis, header inspection, and transparent rules. Our URL model combines character-level TF-IDF with 17 lexical features in a logistic regression classifier. Analysis of the 235,795 URLs in PhiUSIIL revealed pronounced differences in how the two classes were represented: every legitimate example used a simple HTTPS domain format, while 59.9% of phishing URLs included a path and 51.3% used HTTP. A classifier trained on raw URLs achieved 99.71% test accuracy, yet incorrectly marked 26 of 30 ordinary legitimate links as phishing. To limit reliance on these patterns, we trained a second classifier on 197,591 unique registered domains. On held-out domains, it achieved 86.02% accuracy, a ROC-AUC of 0.892, and 89.02% phishing precision. We then combined its predictions with URL-pattern checks, NLTK-based email cues, and SPF, DKIM, and DMARC evidence in a Flask prototype that reports a risk score and supporting reasons. The results show why dataset composition and realistic tests matter as much as headline accuracy when evaluating phishing detection.

publications.title: Robust Markov Decision Processes: An Introduction Using Convex Optimization and Game Theory
publications.abstract: The goal of these notes is to provide a unified and rigorous introduction to robust sequential decision-making. We offer a self-contained introduction to the main results in the field. After a concise introduction to MDPs we introduce robust MDPs with general uncertainty sets, before focusing on rectangular models of uncertainty. We make a significant effort to show connections between robust MDPs and several other popular models for sequential decision-making: MDPs with uncertain rewards, Multi-Objective MDPs and Pareto optimality, MDPs with time-varying uncertain parameters, non-rectangular robust MDPs, stochastic games, distributionally robust MDPs, and risk-averse MDPs. Having all these results in one place, within a single unifying formalism, will hopefully be useful for researchers who want to start working on this topic. The exposition combines operator and fixed point approaches, convex optimization (more specifically, duality in saddle-point problems), and game-theoretic arguments. The latter identifies robust MDPs with a certain type of two-player game; this helps build useful intuition, especially when constructing counterexamples.

publications.title: Polynomial $(2α+\varepsilon)$- and Quadratic $4$-Approximation Algorithms for the Biased Traveling Salesman Problem in Bipartitioned Networks
publications.abstract: The traveling salesman problem (TSP) is one of the fundamental problems in combinatorial optimization that asks for a minimum-cost Hamiltonian cycle in a complete undirected graph with $N$ vertices. For the metric TSP, where edge costs satisfy the triangle inequality, a long line of work has produced constant-factor approximation algorithms, culminating in the best-known approximation ratio $α<3/2-10^{-36}$. The biased TSP (BTSP) generalizes the metric TSP to bipartitioned networks: the vertex set is partitioned into two subsets, edge costs satisfy the triangle inequality within each subset, while edges crossing the partition may violate it by a certain bias factor. This model captures heterogeneous routing scenarios in which distances are metric only locally but may be distorted across different regions or vertex types. Previously, the only known result for the BTSP was a $7/2$-approximation algorithm with running time $O(N^3)$. In this paper, we present two new approximation algorithms that significantly improve the state of the art. The first achieves an approximation ratio of $2α+\varepsilon$ (strictly less than $3$) in polynomial time $N^{O(1)}$ for any constant $\varepsilon>0$, where the exponent grows at least linearly with $1/\varepsilon$. The second achieves a $4$-approximation in only $O(N^2)$ running time, reducing the previous cubic-time bound by a full polynomial factor. These advances directly support emerging networked systems---including multi-tier 6G architectures and hybrid quantum-classical networks---where cross-region transitions incur biased and non-metric overheads.

publications.title: EviRank-ICH Commons Metadata: Sources, Automatic Evidence Labels, Queries and Evaluation Partitions
publications.abstract: Metadata accompanying EviRank-ICH, an evidence-aware video retrieval study. The release contains 4,437 collection-specific segment records from 637 distinct Wikimedia Commons source pages, including source provenance and rights information, automatic evidence labels, compiled queries, grouping and fold assignments, same-item task membership, and source-disjoint refit masks. Version 1.1.1 retains all CSV content from Supplemental Data S1 version 1.1 and updates release documentation. All released evidence labels are automatic; raw human-review data are not included. Study-created contributions are licensed under CC BY 4.0; third-party rights remain unchanged. The package contains no code, model weights, embeddings, videos, images, restricted documentary records, or raw human-review returns. QVHighlights and COIN are not redistributed. The associated manuscript is under resubmission; this release is a dataset, not a publication of the manuscript.

publications.title: Super Intelligence Optimization (SIO v1.0): Algorithmic Discovery Protocols for Autonomous B2B SaaS Web Agents
publications.abstract: Modern B2B SaaS procurement has shifted from traditional human-led search to autonomous agent discovery. Buyers increasingly rely on Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT Search, Perplexity, and Claude to execute vendor research, synthesize feature comparisons, and calculate ROI. Super Intelligence Optimization (SIO) is an evidence-led operating framework engineered to connect traditional search architecture with the token-constrained ingestion protocols of answering engines. This paper defines the baseline SIO architecture required to transition enterprise web platforms from human-only indexing to autonomous agent discovery, maximizing Share of Model (SoM). Canonical Entity & Architecture: https://rakesh.work/

publications.title: Hypertension treatment geography in Korea, 2011-2024: code and district-year data
publications.abstract: Code and district-year data for the manuscript "Persistent north-south geography of age-standardized hypertension care and within-district changes in public sports facility density across 229 Korean districts, 2011-2024" (submitted to Hypertension Research). Includes the analytic panel (3,206 district-years), age-standardized expected counts, adjacency graph, all result tables, analysis scripts (R-INLA, Python), and the scripts that generate every number, table, and figure in the manuscript and Supplementary Information. All inputs are public aggregated statistics. Files are restricted during peer review and will be made public on acceptance. The archive is split into parts; see HOW_TO_OPEN.txt.
